_comment: Canonical source roster for the Daily Cyber Briefing. The 6 AM scheduled task reads this file to build the briefing and APPENDS newly vetted sources here over time. Categories: breaking | investigative | threatintel | vulnfeeds | aisecurity. Tiers: core | strong | aifocus. Do not remove the seeded core sources without reason.

discoveryRules.criteria: Add only sources that are (1) reputable and editorially credible, (2) primarily original reporting/research rather than aggregation, (3) actively publishing in 2026, (4) clearly relevant to cybersecurity or AI/LLM security, and (5) not already present (match by domain). Prefer primary sources that break original stories. When unsure, log as a candidate instead of adding.

sources.name: Pillar Security

Primary original research with hands-on C2/honeypot data; no qianxin.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: SentinelOne (SentinelLABS)
sources.note: SentinelLABS research team; original macOS/APT malware analysis and attribution.
sources.rationale: Published the original technical breakdown of today's macOS.Gaslight DPRK backdoor (Phil Stokes) — the first malware seen prompt-injecting AI triage agents. Consistent primary macOS/DPRK research (NimDoor, BONZAI family); no sentinelone.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Calif.io
sources.note: Vulnerability-research team that discloses original CVEs, including AI-assisted discoveries with PoCs.
sources.rationale: Discovered and published the original disclosure and PoC for today's Squidbleed (CVE-2026-47729), a 29-year-old Squid proxy heap over-read found with AI assistance (Claude Mythos Preview); responsibly coordinated with the Squid project. Primary vuln research, not aggregation; no calif.io domain in the roster.

sources.name: SOCRadar
sources.note: Threat Research Unit (STRU) that runs original dark-web and exposure investigations and ships free checker tools.

Primary original research, not aggregation; no socradar.io domain in the roster.

sources.name: Security Discovery (Bob Diachenko)
sources.note: Researcher who first-hand discovers exposed databases and misconfigured servers, often ahead of broad coverage.
sources.rationale: Bob Diachenko first flagged the exposed FortiBleed attacker server behind today's ransomware-pipeline story, and has a long documented track record of original breach discovery (MOAB 26B records, 8.7B-record Chinese leak, 4.3B database). Primary investigative discovery, not aggregation; no securitydiscovery.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Sysdig (Threat Research Team)
sources.note: Cloud/runtime threat-research team (Sysdig TRT) that captures live attacks with honeypot/runtime telemetry and publishes original incident breakdowns with IOCs.
sources.rationale: Its TRT published the original research on today's lead AI story — JADEPUFFER, the first documented end-to-end LLM-driven ransomware operation (Langflow CVE-2025-3248 to database extortion) — with full payload analysis, timestamps and IOCs. Documented original-research track record (LLMjacking coinage, Langflow CVE-2026-33017 campaign, agentic container escape). Primary hands-on research, not aggregation; no sysdig.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Blackpoint Cyber
sources.note: MDR provider with an APG (Adversary Pursuit Group) that publishes first-party intrusion analysis and malware breakdowns.
sources.rationale: Its researchers (Nevan Beal, Sam Decker) discovered and published the original analysis of today's Avalon modular framework and the new CrownX ransomware — full kill chain, EDR-evasion set and AI-assisted-development assessment — ahead of broad coverage. Primary threat research, not aggregation; no blackpointcyber.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: runZero Research
sources.note: Exposure-management research team (led by ex-CISA vulnerability chief Tod Beardsley) that discloses original CVEs in widely-embedded components and runs its own CNA.
sources.rationale: Discovered and published the original disclosure of today's seven FatFs embedded-filesystem flaws affecting millions of RTOS devices (cameras, drones, ATMs, crypto wallets); documented original-research track record (SSHamble SSH research, runZero CNA, structured 60-day CERT/CC disclosure). Primary vuln research with deep protocol/fingerprint analysis, not aggregation; no runzero.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Ransom-ISAC
sources.note: Ransomware-focused ISAC that reconstructs extortion cases first-hand from leaked negotiation chats and on-chain payment tracing.
sources.rationale: Rakesh Krishnan's original Ransom-ISAC case study behind today's lead story reconstructed the Kairos ~$1M data-theft extortion of a U.S. county (Union County, Ohio) from a leaked negotiation chat and the Bitcoin trail (Bybit/OKX/BELQI), ahead of broad coverage; consistent original leak-analysis research (The Gentlemen ransomware leak analysis). Primary investigative research, not aggregation; no ransom-isac.org domain in the roster.

sources.name: Sekoia TDR
sources.note: Sekoia Threat Detection & Research team; original malware/campaign analysis with IOCs and infrastructure tracking.
sources.rationale: Its TDR team (with YesWeHack) ran the original investigation behind today's ChocoPoC story — analyzing seven trojanized CVE-PoC repos, the PyPI dropper chain and the Mapbox DNS-over-HTTPS dead-drop C2 — ahead of broad coverage; long-running French threat-intel firm with consistent primary research (Aurora Stealer, GootLoader, ClickFix tracking). Primary original research, not aggregation; no sekoia.io domain in the roster.

sources.name: Armadin
sources.note: AI-native offensive-security firm (ex-Mandiant leadership) whose researchers publish hands-on agent/AI-tool attack chains.
sources.rationale: Nick McClendon's original research behind today's AI story detailed a full sandbox escape reaching root inside Claude Cowork's Hyper-V VM (USERENV.dll sideload into signed claude.exe + CoworkVMService RPC abuse), responsibly disclosed to Anthropic; the firm is led by Kevin Mandia and Mandiant founders and focuses on autonomous AI red-teaming. Primary offensive AI research, not aggregation; no armadin.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Zscaler ThreatLabz
sources.note: Zscaler's threat-research org; analyzes cloud telemetry at scale and runs its own AI-agent red-team experiments.
sources.rationale: Published the original indirect-prompt-injection research behind today's lead AI story — CSS-hidden and JSON-LD-buried web prompts that tricked 4 of 26 tested LLM agents (incl. Llama and Gemini variants) into autonomous crypto payments and typosquat trust — tested with its own in-house agent harness across SEO-poisoned sites. Documented track record of zero-day discoveries and annual ransomware/AI-security reports. Primary original research, not aggregation; no zscaler.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Synacktiv
sources.note: French offensive-security/pentest firm that discloses original CVEs and unauthenticated RCE chains with deep technical writeups.
sources.rationale: Discovered and published the original unauthenticated-RCE research behind today's lead vuln story — an unpatched, un-CVE'd Argo CD repo-server flaw that can fully compromise a Kubernetes cluster — after 18 months of unresolved vendor disclosure; documented track record of 300+ public vulnerability disclosures (Livewire, BizTalk360, Snipe-IT, Citrix Provisioning Services) and Pwn2Own research. Primary technical research, not aggregation; no synacktiv.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Aikido Security
sources.note: AI-assisted AppSec/pentesting vendor that discloses original CVEs with deep technical write-ups.
sources.rationale: Promoted from candidate: a month after its original decade-old phpBB auth-bypass discovery (CVE-2026-48611), published a full technical write-up plus a second related CVE (CVE-2026-48612) on July 3, honoring phpBB's requested 4-week embargo. Sustained cadence and embargo discipline over ~3 weeks resolves the 2026-06-16 'watch for independence' concern; primary vuln research, not aggregation.

sources.name: Proofpoint
sources.note: Threat Research team publishing original APT/campaign analysis with IOCs and attribution.
sources.rationale: Its Threat Research team has tracked UNK_MassTraction, a suspected China-aligned cluster exploiting Roundcube n-day flaws (CVE-2024-42009, CVE-2025-49113) against US/Canadian university physics and national-security researchers, since May 2026 — original hands-on campaign research (IceCube stealer, VShell backdoor analysis) ahead of broad coverage. Long-established, well-resourced threat-intel vendor with a deep original-research track record; no proofpoint.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Varonis Threat Labs
sources.note: Data-security research team with a sustained track record of original AI-platform and SaaS vulnerability disclosures.
sources.rationale: Published the original 'Rogue Agent' research disclosing a shared-execution-environment flaw in Google Dialogflow CX (reported Nov 2025, fixed Jun 2026) that could let one edit permission compromise every AI chatbot agent in a GCP project. Consistent original AI-security disclosure cadence (SearchLeak in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Reprompt in Copilot Personal, Cookie Bite Azure MFA bypass). Primary hands-on research, not aggregation; no varonis.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: TechCrunch (Security)
sources.note: Zack Whittaker's security desk; original breach reporting, frequently obtains primary source documents (breach notices, court filings).
sources.rationale: Broke today's lead breach story — the 6.99M-record AssuranceAmerica driver's-license breach — after obtaining and reviewing the actual data breach notification letters via the Indiana and Maine AG offices, ahead of broad coverage. Long documented track record of original security-lapse discoveries (hotel check-in systems, prison payphone providers, UK visa portal, Texas DMV). Primary investigative reporting, not aggregation; surprising gap in the roster given its influence.

sources.name: CERT Coordination Center (CERT/CC)
sources.note: Carnegie Mellon University's vulnerability coordination center; publishes original advisories, including unpatched/uncoordinated disclosures when vendors don't respond.
sources.rationale: Independently discovered and disclosed today's undocumented Tenda firmware backdoor (CVE-2026-11405) and an HP Deskjet 2800 unauthenticated API-exposure flaw (CVE-2026-13753) after being unable to coordinate with either vendor. Long-established, authoritative CNA with a deep original-research track record; no cert.org/kb.cert.org domain in the roster.

sources.name: Nebula Security
sources.note: AI-driven vulnerability-research lab (VEGA bug-hunting tool) with a continuously updated 885+ entry disclosure catalog.
sources.rationale: Its VEGA team discovered and published the original disclosure of today's lead vuln story, GhostLock (CVE-2026-43499), a 15-year-old Linux kernel futex use-after-free giving root and container escape, with a full technical writeup, open-source PoC and a $92,337 Google kernelCTF award. Primary technical vuln research, not aggregation; no nebusec.ai domain in the roster.

sources.name: AI Now Institute
sources.note: Independent, non-corporate-funded AI policy and research institute now publishing hands-on technical exploit research alongside its policy work.
sources.rationale: Published the original 'Friendly Fire' exploit brief behind today's lead AI story, demonstrating that Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex can be hijacked into executing attacker payloads while performing defensive code review, with a transferable working PoC (Boyan Milanov, Heidy Khlaaf). Primary technical AI-security research, not aggregation; no ainowinstitute.org domain in the roster.

sources.name: Sand Security
sources.note: AI-runtime security research team (formerly Koi Security) publishing original disclosures on AI-infrastructure and supply-chain vulnerabilities.
sources.rationale: Its research team discovered and disclosed 'WriteOut,' the critical cross-tenant session-isolation flaw in Writer AI behind today's AI story, coordinating the fix with the vendor before publishing a full technical writeup. Primary hands-on AI-infrastructure vuln research, not aggregation; no sandsecurity.ai domain in the roster.

sources.name: Manifold Security
sources.note: AI-agent runtime-security research team (AIDR platform) founded by the creators of the LLM Guard open-source firewall.
sources.rationale: Disclosed the original ClaudeBleed-linked bypass behind today's lead AI story — reported to Anthropic on May 21 and re-verified as unpatched across all eight subsequent Claude for Chrome releases; also published the earlier spoofed-git-identity AI-code-reviewer research referenced in the Ghostcommit writeup. Primary hands-on AI-agent security research, not aggregation; no manifold.security domain in the roster.

sources.name: Socket
sources.note: Application-security research team that detects and reverse-engineers npm/PyPI supply-chain compromises in near-real time.
sources.rationale: Detected and analyzed today's Jscrambler npm backdoor (ChaCha20-Poly1305-obfuscated infostealer targeting AI coding-tool configs) within the two-hour compromise window; consistent, prolific original supply-chain research track record (Shai-Hulud, IronWorm, node-ipc). Primary technical research, not aggregation; no socket.dev domain in the roster.

sources.name: Jamf Threat Labs
sources.note: Apple-ecosystem threat-research team publishing original macOS/iOS malware analysis.
sources.rationale: Discovered and published the original technical analysis of 'CrashStealer,' the notarized macOS infostealer behind today's lead breach story, tracking it from a May sample through July in-the-wild detections; sustained original-research track record on macOS/iOS threats (ClickFix/Atomic Stealer, Predator spyware analysis). Primary hands-on endpoint research, not aggregation; no jamf.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Check Point Research
sources.note: 200+ analyst research arm publishing original threat intelligence and annual security reports.
sources.rationale: Published the original 2026 AI Security Report behind today's lead AI story, documenting autonomous AI-orchestrated intrusions and the 87-93%-of-orgs high-risk-AI-interaction finding. Held back as a candidate on 2026-07-05 pending recurrence; today's original report resolves that — 718+ published research articles, no checkpoint.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Okta Threat Intelligence
sources.note: Identity-security research team publishing original phishing/vishing campaign tracking with named threat-actor clusters.
sources.rationale: Discovered and published the original O-UNC-066 research behind today's lead breach story — an operator-controlled vishing campaign hijacking Microsoft Entra passkey enrollment for data extortion, tracked since April with its own leak-site attribution. Primary hands-on identity-threat research, not aggregation; no okta.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: GitGuardian
sources.note: Secrets-detection research team publishing original exposed-credential findings and the annual State of Secrets Sprawl report.
sources.rationale: Its automated alerts first flagged the exposed CISA AWS GovCloud keys behind today's Krebs vuln-hygiene story, nine times over six months before CISA acted; sustained original research track record (State of Secrets Sprawl reports, Shai-Hulud 2 secrets analysis). Primary technical research, not aggregation; no gitguardian.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: CEREBLAB
sources.note: Independent AI-safety researcher publishing wire-level (mitmproxy packet-capture) analyses of what AI coding tools actually transmit.
sources.rationale: Published the original wire-level analysis (posted to a reproducible GitHub gist, cereblab.com) behind today's lead AI story proving xAI's Grok Build CLI uploaded entire tracked Git repositories plus secrets/history to a Google Cloud bucket — 27,800x the data the task needed — despite xAI's 'nothing transmitted' privacy claim. Primary hands-on AI-tool security research with reproducible methodology, not aggregation; no cereblab.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Wiz Research
sources.note: Cloud-security research team of veteran white-hat hackers publishing original cloud/AI isolation and supply-chain vulnerability disclosures.
sources.rationale: Discovered and published the original 'GhostApproval' research behind today's AI story — a trust-boundary/symlink flaw letting malicious repos trick six major AI coding assistants (Amazon Q, Claude Code, Cursor, Google Antigravity, Windsurf, Augment) into writing files outside their sandbox via a spoofed approval dialog. Documented original-research track record (Replicate AI-as-a-Service critical vuln, GitHub RCE CVE-2026-3854). Primary hands-on research, not aggregation; no wiz.io domain in the roster.

sources.name: Defused
sources.note: Honeypot-as-a-service threat-intel firm that detects pre-disclosure zero-day exploitation via globally distributed decoy sensors.
sources.rationale: Its honeypot telemetry has repeatedly surfaced active exploitation ahead of vendor confirmation — first flagging in-the-wild attacks on the Cisco Unified CM SSRF (CVE-2026-20230) and publishing original SharePoint exploit-intelligence writeups behind this week's CISA SharePoint warning, plus prior pre-disclosure catches (CVE-2026-35616 FortiClient EMS days before Fortinet's advisory). Primary original telemetry-based research, not aggregation; no defusedcyber.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Tracebit Research
sources.note: AI-agent deception/canary research team publishing hands-on offensive-AI benchmarking with reproducible cyber-range methodology.
sources.rationale: Published the original 'Context Bombs' research behind today's AI story — testing defensive prompt injection against five frontier AI-attacker models (Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GLM 5.2, DeepSeek 4 Pro, Kimi K2.6) across 152 runs in a live AWS cyber range, cutting agent attack success from 91% to 15%; builds on its May 2026 951-run AWS cyber-range benchmark (10 models reaching admin in an average of 14 minutes). Primary hands-on AI-security research with rigorous, repeated methodology, not aggregation; no tracebit.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Volexity
sources.note: Incident-response firm publishing original nation-state threat research and detailed intrusion analysis.
sources.rationale: Original source behind today's active-threat coverage; top-tier hands-on IR/threat-intel reporting, not aggregation; volexity.com not previously in roster.

sources.name: Cloudflare Blog
sources.note: Vendor security research and DDoS/attack-trend reporting from Cloudflare's global network vantage.
sources.rationale: Original primary-source vendor research cited in today's stories; publishes firsthand attack-trend and mitigation data; cloudflare.com not previously in roster.

sources.name: Searchlight Cyber (Assetnote)
sources.note: Research team (Assetnote) that discloses original pre-auth RCE/sandbox-escape vulnerabilities in enterprise SaaS and widely-deployed CMS platforms.
sources.rationale: Discovered and originally disclosed two of today's lead vuln stories: the ServiceNow AI Platform sandbox-escape RCE (CVE-2026-6875, CVSS 9.5, reported to the vendor in April) and the 'wp2shell' unauthenticated WordPress Core RCE chain (CVE-2026-63030/CVE-2026-60137, found by researcher Adam Kues). Primary vulnerability research, not aggregation; no slcyber.io domain in the roster.

sources.name: Cato Networks (Cato CTRL)
sources.note: Cato CTRL threat-intelligence team publishing original hands-on tracking of underground AI-jailbreak and offensive-AI tool development.
sources.rationale: Published the original research behind today's lead AI story, tracking the Russian-speaking threat actor 'Trim' from a March forum jailbreak tutorial to a commercially marketed 'AI Pentest Checker' platform built on jailbroken Claude Opus and a leaked frontier-model system prompt, with named forum handles and a documented four-month timeline. Primary hands-on threat research, not aggregation; no catonetworks.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: KELA Cyber Threat Intelligence
sources.note: Dark-web/cybercrime intelligence firm that unmasks and attributes threat actors using infostealer-log and underground-forum evidence.
sources.rationale: Its research first attributed the ByteToBreach persona behind today's Romania land-registry wipe to a named individual (Zakaria Mahdjoub) using infostealer-log and browser-cookie evidence, and has tracked the actor's prior breaches of Sweden's e-government portal and other government targets since 2025. Primary attribution research, not aggregation; no kelacyber.com domain in the roster.

sources.name: Google DeepMind Blog
sources.note: Google's AI research lab; publishes original vulnerability-hunting model releases and AI-agent-security research alongside a sustained 'Responsibility & Safety' cadence.
sources.rationale: Original source behind today's lead vendor story — 'Introducing Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber,' a gated vulnerability-discovery-and-patching model restricted to governments and trusted partners over dual-use risk, published the same week as its 'Securing the future of AI agents' and 'Investing in multi-agent AI safety research' posts. Primary technical AI-security research, not aggregation; no deepmind.google domain in the roster.

sources.name: Forescout Research (Vedere Labs)
sources.note: Forescout's dedicated threat-and-vulnerability research division; runs a Global Cyber Intelligence Dashboard drawing on 30 billion telemetry datapoints from deployed IT/IoT/OT/IoMT devices.
sources.rationale: Published the original 2026 H1 Threat Review behind today's vendor story — 37,137 newly published vulnerabilities (+51% YoY), 4,544 ransomware claims (+25%), 103 active ransomware groups, and its own tracking of 1,033 threat actors and 5,700+ hacktivist Telegram claims. Decade-long track record of original IoT/OT/IoMT research (Sierra:21); primary data, not aggregation; no forescout.com domain in the roster.
